events.help: Show sub-protocol number along with single-character identifier (useful when observing raw or unknown protocols).
Print a timestamp in the form of +S.UUUUUU, indicating the delta between packet matches.  Specify a second time to indicate the delta since the first packet match.
events.previous_help: Print a timestamp in the form of +S.UUUUUU, indicating the delta between packet matches.

events.help: Do not try to drop privileges to the DROPPRIVS_USER (specified at build-time). ngrep makes no effort to validate input from live or offline sources as it is focused more on performance and handling large amounts of data than protocol correctness, which is most often a fair assumption to make.  However, sometimes it matters and thus as a rule ngrep will try to be defensive and drop any root privileges it might have. There exist scenarios where this behaviour can become an obstacle, so this option is provided to end-users who want to disable this feature, but must do so with an understanding of the risks.  Packets can be randomly malformed or even specifically designed to overflow sniffers and take control of them, and revoking root privileges is currently the only risk mitigation ngrep employs against such an attack.  Use this option and turn it off at your own risk.

events.help: Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.
Colorize matches in packet contents output.
Dump packet contents as both hexadecimal and ASCII.
events.previous_help: Dump packet contents as hexadecimal as well as ASCII.

events.help: Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.
Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.

Resolve container IP addresses to their Docker or Podman container names. When enabled, IP addresses are displayed as in packet output.  If the Docker or Podman socket is accessible, ngrep uses the Events API for real-time container tracking.  Otherwise, it falls back to CLI-based polling with a 30-second cache TTL.  This feature can be excluded at build time with

-A.help: is dump num packets after a match

-C.help: is colorize matches in packet contents output

-D.help: is replay pcap_dumps with their recorded time intervals

-F.help: is read the bpf filter from the specified file

-I.help: is read packet stream from pcap format file pcap_dump

-M.help: is don't do multi-line match (do single-line match instead)

-O.help: is dump matched packets in pcap format to pcap_dump

-P.help: is set the non-printable display char to what is specified

-R.help: is don't do privilege revocation logic

-S.help: is set the limitlen on matched packets

-T.help: is print delta timestamp every time a packet is matched specify twice for delta from first match

-U.help: Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.

-W.help: is set the dump format (normal, byline, single, none)

-X.help: is interpret match expression as hexadecimal

-c.help: is force the column width to the specified size

-d.help: is use specified device instead of the pcap default

-n.help: is look at only num packets

-p.help: is don't go into promiscuous mode

-q.help: is be quiet (don't print packet reception hash marks)

-r.help: is resolve container names for Docker/Podman IPs

-t.help: is print timestamp every time a packet is matched

-u.help: is show payload as UTF-8 characters

-w.help: is word-regex (expression must match as a word)

-x.help: is print in alternate hexdump format
